title: Bounded drift recursion
rationale: The proof claims that the product of (1 + 1/n) over n = 1..m stays near 1 because the factors tend to 1, but the product telescopes to (m + 1)/1 and diverges. The statement itself is refuted by the admissible equality sequence x_n = n: x_1 = 1, x_{n+1} = (1 + 1/n) x_n, and sup_n x_n is infinite, not at most 2.
note: A passing response must locate the bounded-product claim on lines 14-16 and refute the statement; declaring the proof valid, or the statement established, fails.
